Black Friday Bangers: Here Are Five Brands With Some Wild Sales on Their "Death Machines"
21 photos
Photo: Autoevolution | Florin Profir
Over the past couple of years, there has been an explosion in one particular vehicle. It’s not the car, or the bicycle, but rather, the e-scooter. This mobility solution has gained massive traction and with good reasons: they’re nimble, easy to use, and often, pretty darned affordable. Well, with Black Friday sales lighting up all around the world, that “affordable” is about to transform into a “steal.”
Ah, the good old Black Friday, an event that people look forward to time and time again and year after year, and who can blame us: it can be the best time to snag that something you’ve always wanted and at a price that you won’t see again until next year, if ever.
Well, e-scooter brands are also hopping in on the action , slashing prices on some of their most significant machines, and that’s what we’re here to explore. I’ve chosen five of my favorite brands that are currently slashing prices on their beasts, marking it as the perfect time to leave your car at home, if only for a few tasks each day.
Ausom First up on our list of brands that are really hitting the Black Friday sauce is none other than Ausom, a brand whose lineup I have literally decimated in my tests and a brand that simply hits the sweet spot in so many ways, not to mention giving the market what it wants.
Photo: Ausom Ausom is really dropping prices off on their e-scooters, with tried and tested beasts like the DT2 Pro going for as little as $1,100, and the L2 Max Dual Motor and GoSoul 2 Pro, flying off the shelf for a reduced $850.
Keep in mind that the SR1 and F1 Max are also seeing price cuts, e-scooters that I haven’t had the pleasure of testing just yet because when Ausom has then in stock, they’re gone instantly! They too are seeing price cuts of at least $100.
Segway Up next, we have the one and only Segway, a brand that the entire world has heard of . They to are dropping rates quite drastically, with the Max G3 Plus selling for $300 less, or $1,200. Other, entry-level machines, like the F3, is selling for $650, down from a flat $1,000.
Photo: Segway But, there may be no deal better in the Segway aisles, so to speak, than the Max G2, selling for a massively reduced price of $630, down from $1,400. This is the best deal in Segway’s lineup.
Still, not all Segway scooters are up for grabs at lower prices. The latest GT3 Pro SuperScooter is seeing no price cuts, flying off the shelf for $2,700, still. Keep in mind that this is also one of the best-rated e-scooters from the brand, so there are clear reasons why Segway chose to not lower the price.
NanRobot As we move forward with the Black Friday deals, we arrive at NanRobot, a crew that, while it may not be as well-known as Segway or even Ausom, is right up there as one of those brands that kicks out hyper-scooters, insanely fast and powerful machines that we can call upon to actually fly around at speeds as fast as your car.
Their performance lineup of e-scooters is seeing some major price cuts because of Black Friday, with the LS7+ selling for $2,400, reduced $600. It’s their fastest and most expensive e-scooter, capable of reaching 74.5 mph and cranking out a peak of 81 miles of ride time.
Photo: NANROBOT If that’s too much power, check out the X8, going for $389 and limited to just 18 miles of speed but with a range of 25 miles on a full charge.
Now, NanBot also has a simple commuter lineup, with e-scooters now selling for as low as $300, down from $520, so if this is not the time to check in with these brands, I don’t know when is.
Niu Also on this list of essential e-scooter brands to consider for this year’s Black Friday sales includes none other than Niu. This is one of those crews that has always been there in the background, selling their e-scooters all incognito like, but enough to ensure they stay alive, and they have been going strong for several years now.
Photo: NIU Niu prepares their lineup with e-scooters that are even selling for $1,000 their starting price. The carbon fiber KQi Air X is that unit, going for just $1,050, down from $1,900. Another considerable deal is the KQi 300X, one of this crew’s AT rides, and also selling for just $800, down from $1,400. Prices on others are also slashed, so be sure to dive in deeper into their lineup.
Pure Electric Now, the last beast on our list is a team that I don’t expect you to have heard of. Pure Electric is that brand, the one and the same started off by Adam Norris and McLaren. Yes, McLaren can be spotted on an e-scooter, and the Pure x McLaren Flex is selling for £200 less than it was before, going for just £900. The standard Pure Flex is selling for £875 ($1,150), in case you don’t care if it say McLaren on the side of your ride.
Photo: Pure x McLaren Their most affordable option, on the other hand, is the Escape, selling for just £350 ($461), down from £430.
Oh, and pricing for Pure can be found in British Pounds as they’re for sale over in the UK and Europe. Keep in mind, however, that Pure is setting its sights on the US market too. You can start saving up your cash now that you know this.
While these are not the only e-scooter brands out there that are pulling the trigger on amazing deals, they are some of the one’s you should consider. If you have any other brands you’re a big fan of, drop a comment in the section below; it’ll help other readers too.
